messages:
maya: Uploaded draft PRD + RFC for Private Deploy networking. Need quick review of launch gates, acceptance criteria, and edge cases before we lock scope. Link: https://docs.internal/redwood/private-net-rfc-v1

sam: skimmed it. big question: who owns egress IP in customer-managed egress? Do we require BGP always or allow SNAT for customers who can’t run BGP?

lee: i’d support two modes: 'BGP' and 'SNAT'. BGP for customers with proper routing, SNAT for simpler customers. fallback policy: if bgp session flaps, toggle to SNAT + healthchecks and notify ops.

dmitri: rollout gates suggestion: integration tests green (connectivity, egress stability, kv cache warm), canary on 3 pilot customers, p50 latency <120ms, p99 within SLA. must have runbook and rollback steps documented.

irene: security wants: KMS for control plane keys, audit logs exported to customer SIEM optional, HSM option for enterprise. confirm we don’t leak internal metadata on egress headers.

sam: another edge case: overlapping IP ranges between customer onprem and our pod networks. RFC suggests SNAT-to-unique-range + explicit warning to customer. also need a clear DNS handoff section (split-horizon, conditional forwarders).

lee: proposed BGP snippet to include in RFC for operators:
```
neighbor 203.0.113.2 remote-as 65001
neighbor 203.0.113.2 description customer-A-vpc
network 10.200.0.0/22
```
and healthcheck pseudocode: `if bgp_session_state != Established -> withdraw routes & switch to SNAT`

ops-bot: CI: private-networking-integration on branch rfc/priv-net-v1 completed — 12 tests, 0 failures.

dmitri: test matrix we need: BGP up/down, IP overlap, NAT64/translation cases, MTU mismatch, large UDP flows, control-plane rate limits. also chaos tests: drop 50% of BGP keepalives and validate fallback + recovery.

maya: action items captured: @sam update RFC with BGP vs SNAT modes + DNS handoff section; @lee draft fallback state machine + config examples; @irene add security checklist (KMS/HSM/audit); @dmitri author canary test plan. please comment by EOD Friday.

sam: :thumbsup: will do. question: do we expose customer-configurable egress policies (allow-list/deny-list) or keep it platform-managed?

irene: allow customers to configure policies but default to deny outbound except explicit allow-list. audit/log every decision and surface to console.

lee: perf note to call out in PRD: SNAT path adds ~1-3ms per request for large NAT tables in our infra, measure during canary.

maya: noted. i'll add perf callouts and schedule finalize meeting Tue 10am. i'll update doc with above items and ping again.

ops-bot: Reminder: RFC review window is 72h from thread start. If no objections, RFC moves to 'accepted' state after window.
